name: Ithiel
overview: Ithiel was a male member of the tribe of Benjamin, uniquely identified as the son of Jeshaiah. Beyond this specific lineage detail provided in Nehemiah 11:7, little else is recorded about him in Scripture. His profile is concise, grounded primarily in his tribal affiliation and paternal connection.
namesAndTitles: The name Ithiel means 'G-d [El] is with me,' reflecting a meaningful declaration of divine presence. This proper name, as noted in Nehemiah 11:7, conveys a personal acknowledgment of God's nearness, though it was not explicitly given by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Ithiel as the son of Jeshaiah, and it is inferred that Maaseiah was his father. These familial connections root Ithiel firmly within a known lineage in the tribe of Benjamin, but no further family relationships are documented.
scriptureSignificance: Ithiel's significance in the biblical narrative lies in his genealogical mention, which situates him within the post-exilic community of Benjamin. His identification as Jeshaiah's son highlights the continuity of God's people following the return from exile. While not prominent in events, his presence in Nehemiah 11:7 underscores the faithful remnant's restoration and organization under God's providence.
